name: FreeGEM
tagline: GEM lives on — a desktop dithered from gray and blue.
description: FreeGEM is the community-maintained, open-source continuation of Digital Research's GEM (Graphics Environment Manager), the 1980s GUI that dressed up DOS and the Atari ST. Like the hardware it grew up on, it fakes its desktop color by dithering — checkerboarding gray (#a8a8a8) and pure blue (#0000ff) in equal measure. Averaged as pixels that blends to #5454d4; averaged in linear light it becomes the gamma-corrected #7a7ad9.

colors.name: Dithered Blue (Averaged)
colors.note: The FreeGEM desktop. There's no single color for it — the desktop is dithered, checkerboarding gray (#a8a8a8) and blue (#0000ff) in an even 1:1 pattern. This is the conventional pixel average of the two; averaging in linear light instead gives the gamma-corrected #7a7ad9.

colors.name: Dithered Blue (Gamma-Corrected)
colors.note: The same dithered desktop, averaged in linear light and gamma-corrected — a lighter, airier blue. The simpler pixel average is #5454d4.

colors.name: Stone Gray
colors.note: One of the two colors the FreeGEM desktop is dithered from — the gray filling half the checkerboard.

colors.name: Blue
colors.note: One of the two colors the FreeGEM desktop is dithered from — the blue filling the other half of the checkerboard.
